relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: In the 1920s, Goetz obtained a doctorate from the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München.

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: He then joined the Ethnological Museum of Berlin as an assistant curator.

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.object: Kern Institute for Archaeology and Indian History, Leiden University
relations.evidence: There, he became the assistant secretary of Leiden University's Kern Institute for Archaeology and Indian History

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: His superior Jean Philippe Vogel, a reputed Indologist, became his mentor and Goetz started pursuing India-related research.

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: In 1939, the Baroda State's ruler Sayajirao Gaekwad III appointed him as the Director of Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery... Goetz worked at the Baroda Museum until 1953.

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.object: Bulletin of the Baroda State Museum And Picture Gallery
relations.evidence: During this time, he also established the journal Bulletin of the Baroda State Museum And Picture Gallery in 1942

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: He helped set up a Department of Museology at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, and served a professor of art history there.

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: Subsequently, he moved from Baroda to New Delhi, where he became the Director of the National Gallery of Modern Art.

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: In Germany, Goetz became a professor of Oriental Art at the Heidelberg University's Südasien-Institut (South Asia Institute).

relations.subject: Hermann Goetz
relations.evidence: He later served as the Director of history of art at the Institute.
